Always salt your pasta water until it tastes like the sea.
To get the most juice out of lemons or limes, roll them on the counter before squeezing.
Add a pinch of sugar to tomato sauce to cut the acidity.
Let meat rest for at least 10 minutes before slicing to keep the juices locked in.
When baking, room temperature eggs and butter mix much better than cold ones.
Keep your knives sharp; a dull knife is more dangerous than a sharp one.
Roast your spices in a dry pan for a minute to release their full aroma.
If your soup is too salty, drop in a peeled potato to absorb the excess salt.
Always taste your food as you cook, not just at the end!
Use the same wine for cooking that you would drink.
